title: Embedding Caching & Invalidation Strategies
description: Implement efficient embedding caching with Redis, handle cache invalidation for updated documents, and optimize cost for high-throughput embedding pipelines.

data.text: The High Cost of Embeddings: Why Caching is Critical

Embedding generation is one of the most expensive operations in an AI application — both in compute and cost. For text-embedding-3-small, a typical document chunk of 256 tokens costs approximately $0.000002. That seems negligible, but at scale — processing 1 million chunks — it becomes $2.00 per pass. More importantly, the latency of generating embeddings can dominate response time when the same documents are queried repeatedly. A well-designed caching strategy can reduce embedding costs by 80-95%.

Content-based embedding caching uses a deterministic hash of the input text as the cache key. This guarantees that identical text never generates duplicate embeddings. When a document is updated, its hash changes, and the old embedding is naturally orphaned — a separate cleanup job purges expired entries.

data.text: A two-tier caching strategy provides optimal performance: L1 (in-process memory cache) serves hot embeddings with microsecond latency, while L2 (Redis) provides shared caching across application instances and survives restarts. Use a read-through pattern: check L1, then L2, then generate and write to both tiers.

data.text: Use Redis Streams to audit-log all embedding operations for cost tracking and abuse detection. Each embedding generation, cache hit/miss, and invalidation can be streamed to a Redis Stream, which is consumed by monitoring services.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: LLM response caching, embedding caching, and rate-limit coordination are the three primary AI caching use cases
Content-hash keys guarantee deduplication but require versioned invalidation strategies
Two-tier caching (memory + Redis) optimizes both latency and sharing across instances
Set appropriate TTLs: responses 1-7 days, embeddings 1-30 days, rate limits per-minute
Redis Streams can audit-log all AI interactions for cost tracking and abuse detection
data.takeaway: Distributed caching is the bridge from single-instance development to multi-instance production for AI applications, directly affecting cost, performance, and scalability.
